Diarrhea after drinking alcohol ` [Highlight start] happens mainly because alcohol speeds up gut contractions and irritates the lining of your stomach and intestines, preventing your colon from absorbing enough water [Highlight end] ` . Most cases clear up on their own within 24 to 72 hours once you stop drinking and rehydrate.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXhxcdxmXPysPY8WfoGUuCXpsY_l_eSaD8mgsYkMLJPxLaOIU3Ej-i5n9nmclMCbvStrF_l9a_PNfLAYFAYqDFGaqlwc6wX03BzeImZk_PseYrF9NVNfRd191PKZICMVCERywZpmn1t8_FsQGyRiiTh930RQNmf-1J)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXNgmSCsz4-LRErDxRJOU4zU3UTlygCqsim8Y4Ppb3nz0r92UIYL3deDjaebmOweQFceGi6Az8tdmltL2JXVs16Anh9BiBwfbe1MmtfYnEenMRSzsqmtZyF2YviDAkiF65I7kM6walNjHL9-uR_-OB52n1LfI90NU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF12Y4se_PMGinEfLB9HFCvV8FkCqpgTZhVSy6hSUouORubaFcrDbRAJGU17Gvy85snoftcVlHLD5df1LkdE9sEUPPvdVu9_w6q4hZOOVJcae3s3ZHdWh6dq8kXR69KmST-adcXjOycDOUjNuKUhtXwgcZUb9SpSNRgCJRqU8)

### Why It Happens

- **Faster gut transit:** Alcohol speeds up muscle contractions in your digestive tract, pushing stool through before enough fluid is absorbed.
- **Intestinal irritation and fluid shifts:** It irritates the gut lining, triggers inflammation, and draws extra water into the bowel.
- **Gut microbiome changes:** Alcohol can disrupt the balance of helpful and harmful bacteria in your gut.
- **Drink ingredients and mixers:** Beer, sugary mixers, and sweet drinks often add carbs or sugars that worsen loose stools.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXNgmSCsz4-LRErDxRJOU4zU3UTlygCqsim8Y4Ppb3nz0r92UIYL3deDjaebmOweQFceGi6Az8tdmltL2JXVs16Anh9BiBwfbe1MmtfYnEenMRSzsqmtZyF2YviDAkiF65I7kM6walNjHL9-uR_-OB52n1LfI90NU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXhLRa8IxAEWk8NP4cM8Vpm9HP_oqz0ohq-nQ7Dxb1HtRP0w4QH6W7nEQJJY03PSpksVHBN1mknu7voes1cq4cLIYxF7HKN2TJwUmRi-z3EMNCMwlYsTNZ4KBgi-64GkSHn097gf-FHw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXZbdwYQvnkNAIyuQGJHnkN5G-kdqCaaW-oOwfTlaqtUdiq03lk0SbnIWD8nn0d-1KzmRI-SUQtE7f0M26Ps4VECdhgUJxUHI9k6MxDsrDbxDwWLAaVDl23Hkgy0ZGWQIX3A)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1w66tfgWKITRfTaJYDTZTHMwfmULpUGG29-Z1blFDjVWd-0KAZX3HqrOfrdZXYIHCLSq9BeXV4BLucTUIEIqDmaUT1-OCuBWgc21sSV9_UGHn2euPuS_1vljlvqj4d_v9AA535eghcYRAeVkV1tcUU4TIYI3-WmxaOIxCDWPJu5rBAsE4A)

### Common Triggers and Higher-Risk Factors

- Drinking on an empty stomach or binge drinking
- Underlying digestive conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), celiac disease, or Crohn's disease
- Lack of sleep or irregular sleep schedules
- Caffeine, dairy, or greasy foods alongside alcohol[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF16WJbTLO0vHevA7_2KcVlsYlmDmlszaEuRwNINiqUw6zIKkcmsRcZxlTyAk2y4ooxmnr8pw0BkMML7XiD-PzKXVmPWuYUobnIHzD83eWQWt6jZmjxiLpbSjz8vUZ05Xxvv9e24wObD4riwAia17GMHo8s6GnWXBCWEmI7MLu5ZETR69xC-gX)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF12Y4se_PMGinEfLB9HFCvV8FkCqpgTZhVSy6hSUouORubaFcrDbRAJGU17Gvy85snoftcVlHLD5df1LkdE9sEUPPvdVu9_w6q4hZOOVJcae3s3ZHdWh6dq8kXR69KmST-adcXjOycDOUjNuKUhtXwgcZUb9SpSNRgCJRqU8)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXNgmSCsz4-LRErDxRJOU4zU3UTlygCqsim8Y4Ppb3nz0r92UIYL3deDjaebmOweQFceGi6Az8tdmltL2JXVs16Anh9BiBwfbe1MmtfYnEenMRSzsqmtZyF2YviDAkiF65I7kM6walNjHL9-uR_-OB52n1LfI90NU)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1w66tfgWKITRfTaJYDTZTHMwfmULpUGG29-Z1blFDjVWd-0KAZX3HqrOfrdZXYIHCLSq9BeXV4BLucTUIEIqDmaUT1-OCuBWgc21sSV9_UGHn2euPuS_1vljlvqj4d_v9AA535eghcYRAeVkV1tcUU4TIYI3-WmxaOIxCDWPJu5rBAsE4A)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXX_Cf7dra8r9CDoPanwyPUiaGUvRkoalbTwVbt4_hJkxlg6t7PSldQWzuDYIlmq8ysCuDFnWCMLGUeCMBcCLRkIvSqUz_wIkkCgQ-HQTqtpdnmymGnrvNOXAgyQ6WEumhwPI_TGw4c)

### What to Do Now

- **Stop drinking alcohol** until your digestion returns to normal.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF16WJbTLO0vHevA7_2KcVlsYlmDmlszaEuRwNINiqUw6zIKkcmsRcZxlTyAk2y4ooxmnr8pw0BkMML7XiD-PzKXVmPWuYUobnIHzD83eWQWt6jZmjxiLpbSjz8vUZ05Xxvv9e24wObD4riwAia17GMHo8s6GnWXBCWEmI7MLu5ZETR69xC-gX)
- **Replenish fluids:** Sip water, broth, or oral electrolyte solutions. Avoid caffeine and more alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF10Vg3dovnu5QTEGDD4-ntGc7raxvMb5DPkxJ-bA5NpPOXKmLStLEXW3x3GorM28bjwVRLR0UUZmFDAAiAr9_6NYZ8xe_DE9s5WlIn0f9o9l76CBlb99HbDio9l0a6EAGg25X6dvmlUBcCuyxX_lWtEmh7YFzh5958RjpDNM)
- **Eat bland foods:** Try simple options like bananas, rice, applesauce, or toast, and hold off on greasy, spicy, high-fiber, or dairy foods for a bit.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXX_Cf7dra8r9CDoPanwyPUiaGUvRkoalbTwVbt4_hJkxlg6t7PSldQWzuDYIlmq8ysCuDFnWCMLGUeCMBcCLRkIvSqUz_wIkkCgQ-HQTqtpdnmymGnrvNOXAgyQ6WEumhwPI_TGw4c)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF12Y4se_PMGinEfLB9HFCvV8FkCqpgTZhVSy6hSUouORubaFcrDbRAJGU17Gvy85snoftcVlHLD5df1LkdE9sEUPPvdVu9_w6q4hZOOVJcae3s3ZHdWh6dq8kXR69KmST-adcXjOycDOUjNuKUhtXwgcZUb9SpSNRgCJRqU8)
- **Consider over-the-counter relief:** Medications like loperamide or bismuth subsalicylate may help short-term symptoms, though checking with a doctor or pharmacist is smart if you have other symptoms or health conditions. For a thorough breakdown of causes and prevention tips, see the [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXhxcdxmXPysPY8WfoGUuCXpsY_l_eSaD8mgsYkMLJPxLaOIU3Ej-i5n9nmclMCbvStrF_l9a_PNfLAYFAYqDFGaqlwc6wX03BzeImZk_PseYrF9NVNfRd191PKZICMVCERywZpmn1t8_FsQGyRiiTh930RQNmf-1J).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXhxcdxmXPysPY8WfoGUuCXpsY_l_eSaD8mgsYkMLJPxLaOIU3Ej-i5n9nmclMCbvStrF_l9a_PNfLAYFAYqDFGaqlwc6wX03BzeImZk_PseYrF9NVNfRd191PKZICMVCERywZpmn1t8_FsQGyRiiTh930RQNmf-1J)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF12Y4se_PMGinEfLB9HFCvV8FkCqpgTZhVSy6hSUouORubaFcrDbRAJGU17Gvy85snoftcVlHLD5df1LkdE9sEUPPvdVu9_w6q4hZOOVJcae3s3ZHdWh6dq8kXR69KmST-adcXjOycDOUjNuKUhtXwgcZUb9SpSNRgCJRqU8)

### When to See a Doctor
Seek medical care if diarrhea lasts more than 2 to 3 days, or right away if you notice warning signs such as:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1w66tfgWKITRfTaJYDTZTHMwfmULpUGG29-Z1blFDjVWd-0KAZX3HqrOfrdZXYIHCLSq9BeXV4BLucTUIEIqDmaUT1-OCuBWgc21sSV9_UGHn2euPuS_1vljlvqj4d_v9AA535eghcYRAeVkV1tcUU4TIYI3-WmxaOIxCDWPJu5rBAsE4A)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXhxcdxmXPysPY8WfoGUuCXpsY_l_eSaD8mgsYkMLJPxLaOIU3Ej-i5n9nmclMCbvStrF_l9a_PNfLAYFAYqDFGaqlwc6wX03BzeImZk_PseYrF9NVNfRd191PKZICMVCERywZpmn1t8_FsQGyRiiTh930RQNmf-1J)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXNgmSCsz4-LRErDxRJOU4zU3UTlygCqsim8Y4Ppb3nz0r92UIYL3deDjaebmOweQFceGi6Az8tdmltL2JXVs16Anh9BiBwfbe1MmtfYnEenMRSzsqmtZyF2YviDAkiF65I7kM6walNjHL9-uR_-OB52n1LfI90NU)

- Severe abdominal or rectal pain
- Bloody or black, tarry stools
- High fever
- Signs of significant dehydration (such as dizziness, confusion, or very little urination) or unexplained weight loss[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF12Y4se_PMGinEfLB9HFCvV8FkCqpgTZhVSy6hSUouORubaFcrDbRAJGU17Gvy85snoftcVlHLD5df1LkdE9sEUPPvdVu9_w6q4hZOOVJcae3s3ZHdWh6dq8kXR69KmST-adcXjOycDOUjNuKUhtXwgcZUb9SpSNRgCJRqU8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXhxcdxmXPysPY8WfoGUuCXpsY_l_eSaD8mgsYkMLJPxLaOIU3Ej-i5n9nmclMCbvStrF_l9a_PNfLAYFAYqDFGaqlwc6wX03BzeImZk_PseYrF9NVNfRd191PKZICMVCERywZpmn1t8_FsQGyRiiTh930RQNmf-1J)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF16WJbTLO0vHevA7_2KcVlsYlmDmlszaEuRwNINiqUw6zIKkcmsRcZxlTyAk2y4ooxmnr8pw0BkMML7XiD-PzKXVmPWuYUobnIHzD83eWQWt6jZmjxiLpbSjz8vUZ05Xxvv9e24wObD4riwAia17GMHo8s6GnWXBCWEmI7MLu5ZETR69xC-gX)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1w66tfgWKITRfTaJYDTZTHMwfmULpUGG29-Z1blFDjVWd-0KAZX3HqrOfrdZXYIHCLSq9BeXV4BLucTUIEIqDmaUT1-OCuBWgc21sSV9_UGHn2euPuS_1vljlvqj4d_v9AA535eghcYRAeVkV1tcUU4TIYI3-WmxaOIxCDWPJu5rBAsE4A)
